title: The wire between the clients, the hosts (agentsd) and the control plane
description: The source of every type on the wire (#1135). Go (Go/wire) and TypeScript (Web/src/protocol/generated.ts) are made from it by scripts/wire.sh gen; Swift's Model types are written by hand and checked against it (WireSchemaTests).

AccountProfile.description: An account added to a runtime (#840), beside the runtime's own sign-in, which is the Default account and is not one of these. The person picks one when they start a session.

id.description: The host's own name for it. An agent keeps it as accountID.

name.description: What the person called it, such as Work.

signedIn.description: Whether its folder holds a sign-in, as the host read it when it answered.

signedInAs.description: Who it is signed in as, such as an email address, when the runtime's files say.

signInCommand.description: The command that signs it in, in a terminal on the host, for a runtime the app cannot sign in itself (Claude). Absent for one that signs in with runtimes/authenticate.

source.description: Who gave the account (#999): absent or person for one the person added, organisation for an org route, which the person cannot remove.

isDefault.description: The runtime's default account for new sessions (Reaches the Model By, #999). When no account says so, the runtime's own sign-in is the default.

setBy.description: The organisation's policy refuses this account (#999, runtimes.<id>.reach).

AccountReach.description: How an account reaches the model (#840): a sign-in kept in a folder of its own, or (#999) an organisation's route: an org key or a gateway, through the machine's model relay.

folder.description: The folder the runtime is given in its account variable (Runtime.accountFolderVariable).

ActivityToken.description: clients/setActivityToken (#1744): the push token of this device's Live Activity, in hex, for one session it speaks for (#2991: one activity for every turn sent from the device, so one token for several sessions), for the control plane to update it by APNs while the Remote is not running. startedAt is when the session's turn began. No token takes the session out of it.

AddFolderRequest.description: folders/add: the folder, and the project to put it in (#2671). With no project, a folder that names none gets one of its own.

Admitted.description: What either announce is answered with: who the new party now is.

isMuted.description: Mute Notifications (#2003): the session still goes under Needs you and counts in the badge, but sends no push, no Mac notification and no banner. A muted workflow's runs start muted.

branchedFrom.description: The session this one was branched from at one of its prompts (#1658). Until it has a conversation of its own, its runtime reads the record it was given ahead of its first prompt.

fileToSee.description: The last file it showed with show_file that the person has not looked at (#1802): a mark on its row, never a group or a badge. Cleared when the person opens the conversation or marks it read.

continueWhenBack.description: The person asked a chat paused by a spent allowance to carry on when the allowance is back (#1859). At `at` the host sends "continue" in the same chat; a turn that works, any other message, Stop or Archive takes it away.

runningTool.description: While a turn runs, the title of the tool the agent is running now, the newest when more than one is (#1902). Absent while it thinks or replies. It changes only once a new value has held for a second, so a short tool never shows and a short gap between two does not flash. Cleared when the turn ends.

accountID.description: The added account its runtime runs with (#840); absent for the runtime's own sign-in.

auto.description: Set when the agent started on Auto (#2658, FR-007).

clientPermission.description: The agent's own answer to permission requests (#2658, FR-019); absent follows Settings.

levels.description: The shared values the agent runs with now (#2658), where its own settings match one; a field that is absent shows Custom.

voiceHungUpAt.description: When the agent last ended voice mode with hang_up (#2375): the person said they were done talking. A client in voice mode on this chat says the reply, then turns voice mode off.

goal.description: The standing aim its runtime keeps working towards over many turns (#2742), as Codex's and Claude's adapters report it on a session_info_update under _meta.jetbrains.air.goal. Absent when the runtime reports none, or cleared it.

AgentConfigEditorFile.description: A Markdown file under skills, personas or workflows in Agent Configuration.

AgentConfigFile.description: One agent configuration file (#2129), or a deletion tombstone. contents is base64 encoded. Logical time and machine ID resolve concurrent offline edits.

AgentConfigFileRequest.description: One local edit or deletion of an agent configuration file (#2129).

AgentConfigFiles.description: The per-path configuration files and tombstones for a person (#2129).

AgentMachines.description: machines/forAgent: what list_machines shows an agent.

hosts.description: Every machine of the person's, by name, where start_session can start a session (#2887). Absent from an older control plane.

AgentState.description: A state this build does not know reads as `stopped` (Agent's init(from:)), with endedReason `unrecognised`.

AgentStopRequest.description: agents/stop (#2435): the agent, and whether an admin stopped it from the Console, so its owner reads who stopped it. Only a label on the owner's own transcript: whoever sends it could already stop the agent.

AgentsExport.description: What agents/export made (#1001): a .tar.gz in the backup format, read in parts with agents/exportRead. `name` is a file name to save it as.

AgentsExportRequest.description: agents/export (#1001): one agent (`agentID`) or every agent of one folder (`folder`). Give one of the two.

AgentsImportRequest.description: What agents/import takes (#1001): the export sent with agents/importUpload. Its agents come back archived, as a restore brings them; one this machine has, or deleted, is skipped. With `folder`, a folder on this machine (the one whose menu was used, #2389), every agent comes back in that folder; without it, each in the folder it had where it was exported.

AnnounceReply.description: What devices/announce answers: the device's record, with the Mac's relay key beside it when a bridge has registered one (046).

base.description: The SHA-256, in lower-case hex, of the text the edit started from (#1858). When the file on disk is not that text any more, the write is refused with fileChanged and nothing is written. Left out, the text is written whatever is on disk.

AttentionNeed.description: attention/need, unsealed, on a host's channel 0 (R6): a need to offer, or `withdraw`, and the host's whole Needs you count (#1163).

AttentionTurn.description: attention/turn (#1744): a host says that a session's turn moved to a new phase, so the control plane can update each device's Live Activity that speaks for the session by APNs. No words: the phase, and when it ended.

AuditActor.description: Who did something through the control plane (#996, spec 736 FR-039), as the control plane wrote it: never taken from a client. A person and their client, or a bot and the event that started it. On a control plane with one person, the user is always the local owner.

scim.description: A SCIM write: the user is scim:<provider> (#1002).

refresh.description: A suspension by a refused refresh: the user is the suspended person (#1002).

AuditCause.description: The event that started a bot's action (#996).

AuditDays.description: control/setAuditDays (#996): how many days audit entries are kept, 1 to 3,650. The default is 90.

AuditEntry.description: One audit entry (#996): who did what, on which machine, and when. `action` is in words; `method` is the call it came from.

AuditExport.description: audit/export's answer (#996): the entries as JSON lines, oldest first, at most 50,000.

AuditList.description: audit/list's answer (#996): entries newest first, how many days the control plane keeps them, and whether older ones were left out.

admin.description: Whether the caller sees every person's entries.

AuditQuery.description: audit/list and audit/export (#996): a time range and, for an admin, one person. A member sees only their own entries, whatever `user` says.

limit.description: At most this many, newest first; 200 when absent, never more than 1,000.

AuditRefresh.description: A suspension by a refused refresh (#1002, Q1 A): the provider that refused.

AuditSCIM.description: A SCIM write's actor (#1002, D16): the provider and the id of the token it used, never its value.

AuditSink.description: One audit sink (#1001). `address` is tcp://host:port or tls://host:port for syslog, an https:// URL for HTTP. `token`, for HTTP, is sent as a bearer token; it is only ever sent to the control plane, which answers `hasToken` instead.

AuditSinkKind.description: Where an audit sink sends (#1001): syslog (RFC 5424 over TCP or TLS) or HTTP (a POST of JSON lines).

AuditSinkStatus.description: A sink and how this copy of the control plane is sending to it (#1001): entries waiting (at most 10,000), dropped since it started because the queue was full, the last sent, and the last failure.

AuditSinks.description: audit/sinks and audit/setSinks (#1001): the sinks, at most 4. In audit/setSinks, a sink with no `token` keeps the token it had at the same address.

AuditSinksState.description: What audit/sinks and audit/setSinks answer (#1001): each sink and how it is sending.

accountID.description: An added account to sign in (#840); absent for the runtime's own sign-in.

AutoField.description: A field Auto maps (#2658): the model level, the permission mode, the permission requests and the sandbox.

AutoMapping.description: One cell of Settings ▸ Agent Runtimes ▸ Auto ▸ Mappings (#2658): what a level is on one runtime. native is absent when the runtime cannot honour the level.

level.description: A ModelLevel, PermissionLevel, ClientPermissionMode or SandboxChoice, by field.

words.description: The runtime's own words for native, such as Sonnet 5 or Accept edits.

note.description: One line, such as nearest safer: no plan mode.

AutoMappings.description: auto/mappings: every cell, and each runtime's own choices a cell can be set to.

AutoMark.description: How a cell got its value: the shipped map, the nearest value with less access, the person's own, none possible, or a value the runtime no longer offers.

AutoNativeChoice.description: One of a runtime's own settings that a cell of a field can be set to.

AutoOverride.description: The person's own value for one cell (#2658, FR-016).

AutoPick.description: On an Auto agent (#2658, FR-007): the runtime Auto picked, the levels asked for, the native settings given, and why each runtime before it was not used. The runtime never changes in the session.

AutoPreview.description: auto/preview: the runtime Auto would pick now and what it would give, or why none can.

AutoSettings.description: The person's Auto settings (#2658, FR-017), in <settings>/auto.json: the order Auto tries the runtimes in (one not named goes last, in the shipped order), the runtimes it never uses, and their own values for cells.

AutoSkip.description: Why Auto did not use a runtime, in short: out, not signed in, not installed, excluded, no Runtime sandbox.

wait.description: Answer once the backup is made, not at once: a provider's delete waits for it (#1815).

target.description: Where backups go (#1815): this machine's folder, or the control plane's store. Left out is the machine's default: the store for a server linked to a control plane, else the folder.

canUseControl.description: The machine is linked to a control plane, so it can back up to the control plane's store (#1815).

sameDisk.description: The backup folder is on the disk of what it backs up, and not a synced folder (#2139): a backup there undoes a mistake, but is lost with the disk.

BackupStoreCommit.description: A host's backup whose parts are all uploaded: the control plane writes its .json last, then keeps the newest keep of this host's (#1815).

BackupStorePart.description: One part of a backup, at most 8 MiB (#1815): a host's upload, or the control plane's answer to a download.

name.description: On an upload, the backup's name; this host's own folder is the control plane's to say.

Base64.description: Standard base64, with padding: Data in Swift.

BotCaps.description: bots/setCaps (#1761): the bot's caps, and optionally its group.

BotMade.description: bots/make's answer: the bot's user id.

BotMake.description: bots/make (#1761, FR-030): a bot, in a group, with caps. It has no clients and no sign-in; admins approve its machines.

BotStopRun.description: bots/stopRun (#1761, FR-031): an admin stops an agent on a bot's machine, the one way a client acts there.

BranchFromRequest.description: agents/branchFrom (#1658): a new session that goes on from just before the person's prompt `entryID` in `agentID`.

BringBack.description: What folders/bringBack did (#1473): the branches that moved forward or were made, and whether the uncommitted changes were applied.

BringBackRequest.description: Brings a host's branches back into this Mac's repository at `folder` (Bring back from ‹host›…, #1473): fetches the `bundle` upload, moves `branches` forward only, also where a worktree has one checked out, and applies the `patch` upload (the host's uncommitted changes) in `folder`, whose checked-out branch must be `patchOn`. It stops, and changes nothing, when a branch here has commits of its own or a worktree with a branch that moves has uncommitted changes.

BudgetRaise.description: A budget raised for one person for one UTC day (#998, FR-019), kept in the policy and swept the day after.

request.description: The request in Console ▸ Requests it answers.

CapReached.description: control/capReached (#1761, FR-033): to admins, a bot stopped starting work at its own or its group's cap.

CatalogApproval.description: An approval of an MCP server or skill (#2019, M5): for a group, or for one person.

CatalogApprovalList.description: governance/approvals (#2019, M5), an admin's: every approval, by item.

CatalogAsk.description: governance/request (#2019, M5): a person asks for an MCP server or skill, with why.

CatalogDecide.description: governance/decide (#2019, M5), an admin's: approve or refuse a request. Approved with a group, the approval holds for each of its members; with none, for the person who asked.

CatalogItem.description: One MCP server or skill a machine has from a catalogue (#2019, M5): its name, the registry name or catalogue it came from, and its version (a server's version, a skill's commit).

CatalogPerson.description: A person in the catalogue's rows: their id and name.

CatalogRequest.description: A request for an MCP server or skill (#2019, M5). Approved for a group, it is approved at once for every member who asks again.

CatalogRequestList.description: governance/requests (#2019, M5): every request waiting to an admin, and to anyone their own of the last 30 days, oldest first.

CatalogRevoke.description: governance/revoke (#2019, M5), an admin's: take back one approval, for a group or for a person.

CatalogUsage.description: governance/usage (#2019, M5), an admin's: who uses each MCP server and skill, at each version, from what each machine last reported.

CatalogUseRow.description: One item at one version in governance/usage: on how many machines, and whose (at most 50 people named).

CatchUpPart.description: A part this host does not know is left out of CatchUpRequest.parts.

ChannelDKIM.description: ChannelSender.dkim (#1762, FR-037): the DKIM result the email server read for a message, from its own Authentication-Results.

ChannelLink.description: links/list (#1762, data-model.md "Channel link"): a channel identity linked to a person, and who approved it when.

ChannelLinkChecked.description: links/check's answer (#1762): user is the linked person; with none, nothing starts, and refused says why when it is not only that the identity is not linked yet.

ChannelLinkDecide.description: links/approve, links/deny (#1762). An admin approving a request that names nobody names the person in for, and the request goes to them.

ChannelLinkDecided.description: control/linkDecided (#1762): a request ended (approved, denied, expired) or went to another person (sent), so every card for it goes.

ChannelLinkRequest.description: links/requests, control/linkRequested (#1762): a channel identity waiting to be linked. for is the person asked; with none, the admins send it on to a person.

ChannelOpen.description: What a channel on a host's uplink is opened as (ControlWire.ChannelOpen).

actor.description: Who the channel's calls are from, written by the control plane (#996).

ChannelSender.description: links/check (#1762, FR-037), and an MCP event's sender: who sent a channel message. channel is the channel's kind (slack, email), identity the sender on it (for email, the address).

ClientConnection.description: One row of clients/connections: a client connected now, and how.

ClientKind.description: ClientRecord.Kind: a kind a later build added reads as `unknown`.

ClientPairingRequest.description: clients/startPairing: `browser` for the web remote's code (071); a grant an older window sends is not read.

ClientPermissionMode.description: The older autoReview reads as alwaysApprove.

setBy.description: Set when the organisation's mode ceiling is below approving every request: Always-approve is refused, and no agent's requests are answered for the person.

ClientRecord.description: A paired screen, as clients/list says it (ClientRecord).

setBy.description: Set when the organisation's policy refuses this choice (#998, FR-010): a mode above the ceiling, or a model it does not allow.

type.description: "select", "boolean", or a kind this build doesn't know, carried as itself.

ConfigOption.description: ConfigOption (Model/Options.swift), as its encode(to:) writes it: `type` is the kind's wire name, and `options` is a flat list for one unnamed group, else the groups.

Connection.description: The person's sign-in to one provider, as the host keeps it. Never its tokens.

login.description: The account's name on the provider, such as alexec.

installURL.description: Where the person installs the provider's App: a GitHub user token reaches only the repositories where it is installed.

workspace.description: The part of the provider the token reaches, such as a Linear workspace's name, or a self-managed GitLab's host.

expiresAt.description: When a token the host cannot renew ends: a GitLab personal access token's expiry. The person makes a new one before then.

ConnectionEmailRequest.description: connections/sign-in/email (#1780): one IMAP mailbox for the email server. The host signs in once to check it, keeps the app password in its own store, and never logs it or gives it back. The answer is a ConnectionTokenAnswer.

server.description: The IMAP server, such as imap.fastmail.com (imaps:// on 993 when it names no scheme), imap://host for STARTTLS on 143, or with a port.

user.description: Who signs in, usually the mail address.

password.description: An app password made for Agents at the mail provider.

ConnectionProvider.description: A tool the person connects to: GitHub (#1335) and Linear (#1343) with OAuth, GitLab (#1630) with OAuth on gitlab.com or a personal access token on any GitLab, and email (#1780): one IMAP mailbox with an app password.

origin.description: For connections/sign-in from the web page: the page's origin. The hand-back page sends the code to this origin only, by postMessage. Without it, the hand-back page sends the code to agents://oauth/callback (the Mac and the Remote).

ConnectionSignIn.description: A sign-in under way on the host (#1335, #1343). The host keeps the secrets (the device code, the PKCE verifier); a client shows the code or opens the address, and waits.

userCode.description: deviceCode only: the code the person types at verificationURL, such as WDJB-MJHT.

verificationURL.description: Where the person goes: the device page, or the provider's authorize page (with the state and the PKCE challenge, never the verifier).

message.description: Why it failed, in words. Never a token.

ConnectionSignInCompleteRequest.description: What the hand-back page gave the client (#1343): the code and the state, or the provider's error. The host checks the state, then spends the code with its own verifier.

error.description: The provider's error code, such as access_denied.

ConnectionSignInGrant.description: deviceCode: the person types userCode at verificationURL (GitHub), and the host polls. authorizationCode: the person approves at verificationURL in an authentication session (agents:// on the Mac and the Remote, a pop-up on the web page); the hand-back page gives the code back to the client, which gives it to the host with connections/sign-in/complete (Linear).

ConnectionSignInStatus.description: waiting: for the person to approve on the provider's page. connected: done. expired: the code or the sign-in ended. denied: the person pressed Cancel on the provider's page. cancelled: a client stopped it. failed: see message.

ConnectionState.description: connected: the host has a token and renews it. signInAgain: the provider refused the renewal, so the person signs in again.

ConnectionTokenAnswer.description: The connection the token made, or why it made none, in words.

ConnectionTokenRequest.description: connections/sign-in/token (#1630): a personal access token the person made, for a provider with no Agents application there (a self-managed GitLab). The host checks it with the provider, keeps it in its own store, and never logs it or gives it back.

url.description: The provider's address, such as gitlab.example.com (https:// when it names no scheme). gitlab.com when left out.

ConnectorCodespace.description: A GitHub Codespace for a folder's repository (#1591).

ConnectorCodespacesRequest.description: Lists or changes the folder's GitHub Codespaces (#1591).

ConnectorEvents.description: The github events the set-up turned on, and the folder's workflows that start on one of them.

server.description: The mcp.json name that offers them.

ConnectorEventsState.description: on: the github connector is in the folder's or the person's mcp.json, so its events reach this folder. off: not yet (nothing connected, or every GitHub slot skipped). taken: an mcp.json entry not made by Agents already has the name github, and it is left alone. failed: the entry could not be written; message says why.

ConnectorProof.description: The one real thing a slot read: the newest issue or pull request, or the last workflow run.

number.description: The issue or pull request number.

title.description: Its title, or the run's workflow and branch, such as "CI on main".

outcome.description: A run's outcome in a word: passed, failed, running, cancelled.

ConnectorSetup.description: A folder's Connectors set-up (#1336): its GitHub or GitLab repository (#1632), the person's connection to that forge, four slots that each prove themselves with one read, and the events.

repository.description: owner/name on GitHub, or group/project on GitLab, from the folder's git remote (origin first). Absent with no GitHub or GitLab remote.

forge.description: The forge the repository is on, which fills Tasks, Code review and CI: github or gitlab (#1632). Absent is github.

site.description: The repository's host, as the page says it before the repository: github.com, gitlab.com, or a self-managed GitLab's host.

repositoryURL.description: The repository's page on its forge, where the person asks for access when a read is refused (GitLab).

installed.description: Whether the Agents App is installed on the repository. Absent when not known.

repositories.description: How many repositories the connection sees through the App.

done.description: Slots that read or were skipped, of the four.

project.description: The folder's project id (#2669), whose owner or an admin sets Tasks, Code review and CI for every folder in it. Absent when the folder is in no project.

projectName.description: The project's name, as this machine last heard it from the control plane.

ConnectorSetupReading.description: stored: no call to the provider, only what was read before (for a list of every folder). cached: a read at most five minutes old is used again. fresh: read now (Try Again).

ConnectorSkipRequest.description: Skip a slot, or set it up again. Kept in the folder's .agents/folder.json.

ConnectorSlot.description: One slot and what it read. A slot that has read keeps its proof when a later read cannot reach the provider; only a refusal unticks it.

choice.description: What fills it, in words: GitHub Issues, GitHub pull requests, GitHub Actions, This Mac.

message.description: Why a read failed or was refused, in words. Never a token.

repository.description: The repository that fills this slot (#2669): the project's when fromProject, else the folder's own. Absent for workspace and with no remote.

fromProject.description: The folder's project sets this slot (#2669), so it is the same in every folder of the project.

ConnectorSlotKind.description: One slot of a folder's set-up (#1336), in the page's order: tasks (the tracker), codeReview, ci, and workspace (where agents run).

ConnectorSlotState.description: notConnected: the slot comes with a connection that is not there yet. notRead: connected, but not read yet (a stored reading). read: its one read worked (a tick). failed: the read did not reach the provider; message says why. refused: the provider refused the read, so the person grants it on the provider's site. noRemote: the folder has no GitHub or GitLab remote. skipped: the person skipped it; it counts as done.

ConsoleStopAgent.description: console/stopAgent (#2019, M9): an admin stops one agent on any machine of the organisation, as Console ▸ Live Now does.

ContentBlock.description: ContentBlock (ACP/ContentBlock.swift): the protocol's own block shapes, as sent. A block of a kind this build doesn't know is written back as it came, so any other `type` may arrive.

ContinueInNewRequest.description: agents/continueInNew (#999): a new session in the same folder that reads this one and carries on, on another account of its runtime.

accountID.description: The account the new session uses: an added account, an org account (org:<route id>) or default for the runtime's own sign-in. Absent: the runtime's account for new sessions (Reaches the Model By).

auto.description: Continue on Auto (#2658, FR-022): the successor starts on the runtime Auto would pick now, with the session's values. Only for an Auto session.

ContinueWhenBack.description: When a chat paused by a spent allowance carries on by itself (#1859).

at.description: When it sends "continue": the provider's reset time, or the app's next check of the runtime.

resetKnown.description: True when `at` is the time the provider said the allowance resets; false when it is only the app's next check.

ControlAuth.description: The peer's answer: {"auth":…} (ControlAuth.Auth). `kind` is mac, iphone, ipad, browser, host, relay, copy or page.

capabilities.description: The capabilities this client has (#1748). None from a client older than #1748, or from a host, which says its own in host/hello.

page.description: With a `w:<host>` identity (#1480): the port of that host's loopback listener. The socket then carries a page from the loopback origin on port <page>, whose own exchange follows the ok, bound to that origin.

publicKey.description: With an `s:<client>` identity (#995): the key of the client that signs in, X9.63. The exchange's MAC is under the ECDH of it and the control plane's key, as a paired client's is.

ControlClientChanged.description: control/clientChanged: a client paired, renamed, connected or went; nothing says list them all again.

ControlCodeShown.description: clients/startPairing, hosts/startEnroll: the code, until when it works, and for a host the one line to run on the server.

ControlCutOff.description: control/cutOff (#1002, D13): to every client of a suspended person, just before the control plane closes their sockets with 4403 suspended.

ControlEndpoint.description: One place a control plane answers (R16).

ControlHello.description: The control plane's first line of the exchange: {"hello":…} (ControlAuth.Hello).

previous.description: The control plane's key before control/rotate (#997, spec 736 FR-043), for 30 days after: a member that still trusts it proves itself with it, and is given the new key in ok.

ControlInstallProgress.description: control/installProgress: a step of Add a Machine.

capabilities.description: The capabilities this host said in its last host/hello (#1748). None from a host older than #1748.

missing.description: Of the control plane's required capabilities for hosts, the ones this host does not have (#1748). Its state is then needsUpdate.

owner.description: The user who owns the machine (#994).

ControlMoved.description: control/moved: where the control plane is now (T085).

ControlNewKey.description: The control plane's new key (#997, spec 736 FR-043), in ok to a member that proved itself with the previous one. proof is the HMAC of the new key under the member's shared key from the previous one, so only the holder of the previous key could have made it. The member trusts the new key from then on, with no new pairing.

ControlNotice.description: control/notice (#1002): something an admin should know, that no click caused: lastAdminKept, groupSharesOrphaned or removeRequested; words to show, and whom it is about.

ControlPerson.description: Who a client belongs to (#994): its person, their role, and whether they are the local owner.

ControlPush.description: The `agents` key of a push the control plane sends through APNs (#1460), beside an `aps` that says only that an agent needs the person: a ControlPushItem, sealed.

ControlPushItem.description: What a control plane's push carries, sealed whole to the device (#1460): the need, whether to buzz, and the banner's words. No headline is a withdrawal.

publicWeb.description: Where a browser anywhere opens the page, on the control plane's own domain (#1459): its https address, when it serves the page there.

publicViews.description: The origin of the sandbox proxy that draws MCP Apps views on the page at publicWeb (#1484): a second name in front of the same control plane. None when it draws no views there.

capabilities.description: The capabilities the control plane has (#1748).

joinCommand.description: The one line to run on a server so that it asks to join as this client's person, with no code (#994).

organisation.description: The organisation's budgets for this person today, in US dollars and tokens, with any raise (#998, FR-016). Each limit in force is the lower of this and limits.

setBy.description: Set when the organisation's budgets cap this person's own limits, or this person is at a budget today (#998).

DefaultAccountRequest.description: runtimes/setDefaultAccount (#999): a runtime's account for new sessions. accountID default (or absent) is the runtime's own sign-in.

DeletePreview.description: How many archived agents a retention change would delete at once, and the bytes that frees.

DeliveredRoute.description: One org route as a machine gets it (#999, FR-005): the route without its groups, fingerprint and stamps, and each secret sealed with HPKE to the machine's key (SealedEnvelope), info com.alexecollins.agents.orgroute.v2, associated data <route id>|<host id>|<version>|<hex SHA-256 of the route as JSON without sealed>, so a route whose settings changed after delivery does not open. A cloud credential is sent only as a token that ends at expires (Q1 A): awsSession, googleToken or entraToken.

sealed.description: Each secret value, or token, by field.

DetectedServer.description: One host in the ssh config, and what hosts/detect did with it (#429).

Device.description: A paired device (021 US5), as devices.json keeps it.

DeviceAnnouncement.description: devices/announce: this device, and the public half of its key.

DeviceNotification.description: device/changed: the whole record, or that it was forgotten (046).

DomainClaim.description: A claimed email domain (#1002, D8, FR-010): proved by the TXT record `txtValue` at `txtName`, for one org provider. The control plane keeps it at v1/signin/domains/<domain>.json and checks it each day; 7 days of failures take it back to notProved. `sendHere` sends an email at the domain to the provider (signIn/discover); `require` refuses a built-in sign-in at the domain to join, pair or renew (D9).

DomainClaimState.description: Whether a claimed domain's TXT record was found (#1002).

EditQueuedRequest.description: agents/editQueued (#1552): a queued prompt's new words, in its place in the queue.

EditQueuedResult.description: Whether the prompt was still waiting and now has the new words. False: it was sent, or taken back, first.

ElicitationSecret.description: An agent's ask_secret (#2885): one named secret, typed into a masked field. The value goes to the person's secrets.env on the host, never into the record.

EndedReason.description: A reason this build does not know reads as `unrecognised`.

actor.description: Who raised it, when a person's call through the control plane did (#1751, spec 736 FR-040): the actor the control plane gave the call's channel, never taken from the client. None for what an agent, a workflow or the machine did.

EventPattern.description: EventPattern (Model/EventPattern.swift), as its encode(to:) writes it (073): `filters` holds every filter as one string, a list joined by `|` so an older build reads it as a value that never matches, and `anyOf` holds the lists whole. Read `anyOf` over `filters`.

forPerson.description: Only the connected person can carry this on (#3051): review.requested or issue.assigned today. Left out or false for everything else.

FeatureUsage.description: reports/features (#2165): each feature this host counted, a method it serves or an app tool, with its uses in the last 7 and the last `days` days, the least used first. A feature with no use is in it too. Counts only, never what a call said; they stay on the machine. since is the first day counted in the range.

FeatureUse.description: One feature's uses (#2165). clients is who used it: mac, remote, web, agent or workflow.

FileCompletion.description: One thing to write: what the list shows, what goes in the text (the label when left out), and a line about it.

FileCompletionRequest.description: files/complete (#844): what the language server would write at a place in a file, as the editor holds it. line from 1; column from 1, in UTF-16 units as the text views count.

FileCompletions.description: At most 50 completions, in the server's order; reason says why there are none (no server, or none installed).

FileDiagnostic.description: One problem a language server found: where (line and column from 1), how bad (error, warning, info or hint), and what.

FileDiagnostics.description: A file's problems, at most 200, and the server that found them. Reason says why there is no server for it (none installed for the language, or the file too big).

FileDiagnosticsRequest.description: files/diagnostics (#844): what the language server for a file's language says of it, as the editor holds it (text) or as it is on disk.

FileReading.description: FileReading (Model/FileReading.swift), as its encode(to:) writes it: one shape per `kind`.

FindMatch.description: One message that holds the text: where it is in the transcript (its first chunk), and the line it is on.

FindRequest.description: agents/find (#1532): what was said in one chat, prompts and replies, that holds the text, any case.

FindResult.description: The matches, oldest first: the newest `limit` of them. More is true when older ones were left out.

FleetBoard.description: console/fleet's answer (#1804): every machine on the control plane, for an admin.

FleetMachine.description: One machine on Console ▸ Machines (#1804): its hosts/list row, whose it is, and how many of its agents were running when it last listed them. Numbers only, never what the agents said.

ownerName.description: Its person's or bot's name; empty when nobody owns it.

bot.description: Whether its owner is a bot (#1761).

running.description: Its agents running when it last listed them; absent when it never has.

heardAt.description: When it last listed its agents.

project.description: The project id that .agents/folder.json names (#2317). Absent when it names none or one that is not valid.

projectProblem.description: Why the folder is in no project (#2317): .agents/folder.json is not an object, names an id that is not valid, or .agents is a link.

helperLimitsSetBy.description: Set when the organisation's policy caps this folder's helper limits (#998, #64): the lower number is used.

GitCredential.description: A credential for one git command. Never printed, logged or kept.

GitCredentialRequest.description: git/credential, git/fill (#1122): only https, and only the server. `path` is the Go host's, unread by Swift.

GitView.description: GitView (Model/AgentChanges.swift): `{ shared: { since } }`, `{ unavailable: … }` and so on.

iterations.description: How many turns it took towards the goal, where the runtime counts them.

reason.description: Why it last stopped or paused, in the runtime's words.

tokenBudget.description: The tokens it can use on the goal, when it has a budget.

at.description: When the host last heard of it.

GoalStatus.description: Where a goal stands (#2742): active (it can drive more work, whether or not a turn runs now), paused, blocked, limited (a usage or token budget ran out) or complete.

Group.description: A group (#1761, spec 736 FR-027): everyone, or named users. It owns machine providers: only its users see them and start machines from them (FR-028).

source.description: A SCIM group's provider (#1002). Absent for a group an admin made.

role.description: Gives the admin role (#1002, FR-020): its members are admins.

GroupList.description: groups/list (#1761): every group for an admin; for a member, the groups they are in.

GroupRequest.description: groups/remove (#1761): the group. Refused while a machine provider or a bot has it.

GroupRoleSet.description: groups/setRole (#1002, FR-020): mark a SCIM group as giving the admin role, or not (no role).

GroupSet.description: groups/set (#1761): makes a group, or with id changes one. One user is a list of one.

GroupSource.description: Where a group comes from (#1002, FR-019): an org provider's SCIM. Only SCIM changes its members.

GroupsChanged.description: control/groupsChanged (#1761): a group was made, changed or removed.

HandoverMember.description: A member as a copy says it, for the one driving a handover (Handover.Status.Member).

HandoverStatus.description: handover/status: what a copy says of itself, for the one driving a handover to check before each step (R16).

continueWhenBack.description: A helper's turn refused for a spent allowance waits for it at once, as if the person had chosen Continue (#1918). Off unless set.

archiveWhenMerged.description: A session whose pull request merges is archived, when its turn has ended and its worktree has nothing uncommitted (#2886). On unless set.

agentsMayStartOnMachines.description: start_session with a machine starts the session on another of the person's machines without asking first (#2928). Off unless set; only the person sets it, from Folder Settings.

JSONValue.x-ts-type: null | boolean | number | string | JSONValue[] | { [key: string]: JSONValue }

JoinDecided.description: control/joinDecided (#994): a request ended, approved or not, so every card for it goes.

JoinRequest.description: hosts/joinRequests, control/joinRequested (#994): a machine waiting for approval, with the code it shows.

KeepRequest.description: hosts/keep: a request for a stopped host, kept until it is up.

Levels.description: The values a session asks for in the words every runtime shares (#2658). Each is mapped to the runtime's own setting; a native value in startOptions for the same option wins.

LineageCost.description: What was banked under lineage nodes (#2350): a turn's cost, tokens and time, split evenly among the links active when it was banked. turns is a share of turns, so a turn on two nodes is half a turn on each.

limitTokens.description: Fresh input and output, as a limit counts them (#998).

workingSeconds.description: The agent, its tools and others at work.

LineageCostNode.description: One node's banked cost on a machine (#2350), whole, with what its rollups need: the project its ref is in, the issues a PR fixes (ended links too: a PR closed without a merge still counts against its issue, as waste), the milestones it is part of, and how a PR ended. A session's own cost is its turns that had no active link.

project.description: The repo or tracker the node is in: github:alexec/agents, linear, or for a session its folder's repo (folder:<name> without one).

partOf.description: The milestones it is part of, by ref.

outcome.description: A PR's end: merged, closed (without a merge: waste) or reverted (a merged revert: waste). Absent while open. The list is open.

failedChecks.description: A PR's failed CI rounds: checks.failed, once per run and attempt.

firstAt.description: When the machine first banked or noted the node (#2351): the start of the work on it, for lead time.

endedAt.description: When a PR ended (#2351): merged, closed or reverted. Absent while open.

LineageCostRollup.description: lineage/cost (#2350): a node's cost rolled up. own is what was banked on the node itself. total adds its parts: an issue's PRs (the PRs that fix it); a milestone's issues, their PRs and the PRs part of it; a project's every node (kind project, ref github:alexec/agents). waste is the parts' PRs closed without a merge or reverted. unlinked is the parts' sessions: turns with no active link. parts is the nodes added up, newest first, at most 500; limited says there are more.

LineageEndRequest.description: lineage/end (#2348): the link from one node to another by this relationship stops being active now. Nothing is removed: the link keeps its start and gets an end.

LineageGraph.description: lineage/walk (#2348): the nodes the walk reached and the links it went along. limited says the walk stopped at its limit on nodes, so there is more.

LineageLink.description: A typed link in the lineage graph (#2348): from works-on, opens, fixes, started, reviews, closes or part-of to. source is how the host knows it: start, branch, pr-body, helper, agent, person or forge. at is when it started; endedAt is set when it stops being active (a PR merged, a session archived). Both lists are open: a host keeps a relationship or a source it does not know.

LineageLinkRequest.description: lineage/link (#2348): start a link. When the same link is active already, it is the answer, unchanged.

LineageLinks.description: The links of a node, newest first (#2348), or the links lineage/end ended. limited says there are more than the answer holds.

LineageNode.description: A node in the lineage graph (#2348). kind is what it is: issue, pr, session, workflow-run, commit, file, branch or milestone, and the list is open. ref names it apart from any tracker, as <scheme>:<id>: github:alexec/Agents#123, gitlab:group/repo!45, linear:ENG-4, jira:ABC-9, session:<agent id>.

LineageNodeRequest.description: lineage/links and lineage/walk (#2348): a node, and for a walk how many links away to go (1 to 4; 2 when not said: issue, sessions, PRs).

LiveAgent.description: One agent on Console ▸ Live Now (#2019, M9): whose machine, which runtime, its state, since when and its cost so far. No title and nothing it said.

owner.description: The person or bot whose machine it is, by id.

bot.description: Whether the machine is a bot's.

waitsOnOthers.description: It waits for an event or another agent (eventWait), not for its person.

costToDate.description: Its cost so far, by currency.

heardAt.description: When the machine last listed its agents.

LiveBoard.description: console/live's answer (#2019, M9): every agent running now on every machine, as each machine last listed them, for an admin. The most costly first.

MCPLevels.description: The five levels a connector reaches (#1428): tools, events and views from what the server declares, workflows when a ready-made workflow names one of its events, tested when it was tested on a real account.

MacPathRequest.description: mac/reveal, mac/open: a path on the host; app names the app to open it with.

MacTerminalRequest.description: mac/terminal: Terminal, in path if given.

MachineCatalog.description: governance/report (#2019, M5): the MCP servers and skills a machine has from a catalogue, personal and in its folders, at most 500. Sent at start and each hour; each replaces the last.

MachineClient.description: A paired window a host may let in on its local socket (#1118), with the key it proves itself with.

person.description: The person the window belongs to (#994). The host lets it in only when it is the host's own user (FR-020).

MachineClients.description: host/clients: every window paired with the control plane, which a host checks its local socket against (#1118).

user.description: The user the host belongs to (#994). With it, the host lets in only a window whose person is that user (FR-020); without it (an older control plane), every window listed.

MachineEnroll.description: hosts/startEnroll (#1761): with as, a bot's machine code, an admin's only. Without, the caller's own, as before.

MachineFolderSend.description: machines/sendFolder, through host/machines: one step of an agent's start_session with send (#2929), which sends this folder's branch to another of the person's machines first, or of its bring_back (#2947), which brings a branch back from there. Exactly one of state, upload, receive, facts, pack and read; the control plane sends that machine's folders/receiveState, folders/receiveUpload, folders/receive, folders/sendFacts, folders/sendPack or folders/sendRead.

MachineFolderSent.description: What machines/sendFolder's step answered (#2929, #2947): state for state, folder for receive, facts for facts, pack for pack, read for read, none for upload.

MachineHello.description: host/hello, on every connect of an uplink. `implementation` is `swift` or `go` (#1134).

capabilities.description: The capabilities this host has (#1748): each one whose methods it all serves, and the ones it declares. None from a host older than #1748.

MachineInfo.description: One workspace, as its provider last listed it. `state` is running, starting, stopping, stopped or unknown.

hostKeyRenews.description: Its ssh host key is made again at each start, as a Google Cloud workstation's is (#1701): after a Start the control plane made, the first ssh takes the key it is offered and pins it again.

MachineInstall.description: hosts/install (MachineInstall.Request): a server over ssh, with its key, the fingerprint trusted, a tunnel.

MachineJoinAsk.description: POST /v1/join (#994, spec 736 FR-017): a machine with no code asks to join. `person` names whose it is to be, by name or id; with none, an admin approves it.

MachineJoinDecision.description: GET /v1/join/<request> (#994): waiting, or how it ended; `host` once approved.

controlKey.description: Once approved: the control plane's public key, which the machine keeps as a code's would give it.

name.description: Once approved: the control plane's name.

MachineJoinTicket.description: POST /v1/join: the request, the short code the machine shows, and when it ends (10 minutes).

MachinePolicy.description: host/policy (#998, FR-006): to a machine that says host.policy/1, on its channel 0, at each join and within 5 seconds of each change. A signed policy, or none when no policy was ever set.

MachineProjects.description: projects/joined's answer and host/projects (#2669): the projects that this machine's folders name, with their slots, all of them each time.

MachineProviderDraftCall.description: host/providerDraft: a writing agent called one of the writer's tools (#858).

MachineRelease.description: host/release (#2178): the release the control plane names, as X.Y.Z.

MachineSessionCall.description: machines/sessionCall, through host/machines (#2927): an agent's read_session, message_session, stop_session, archive_session, or list_sessions and wait_for_agents status, on a session it started on another of the person's machines with start_session. The control plane sends that machine's agents/fromStarter, with call.from in its own words.

MachineSessionStart.description: machines/startSession, through host/machines (#2887): an agent's start_session on another of the person's machines, by its name. The control plane sends that machine's agents/start.

MachineStatus.description: host/status on channel 0 (#691 US4): each agent working or waiting on a person, and the next scheduled workflow.

MachineUpdate.description: hosts/update (#1766): a host the control plane installed over ssh, updated the same way. The server and its key are given again, as at the install, because the control plane keeps neither; the host's own root and membership stay.

MachineUser.description: host/user (#1761): to a machine on its channel 0, at each join and when its user changes. Its user, their kind, and the labels runs-on: matches (FR-034); for a bot at its cap, until when it starts no work (FR-033).

bots.description: For a person: the names of the bots in their groups (#2027). A runs-on: workflow that names one is heard here, once approved here, and its matches are sent to the control plane, never run here.

MachineUserSettings.description: host/userSettings (#1760, FR-024, FR-025): to a machine, on its channel 0, when it joins and when its user's settings or secrets change. Sent only on the links of that user's own machines. secrets is every secret the user has: a name missing from it was removed.

MachineWorkspaceCall.description: host/machines, for an agent there: who asked, for the log, and its call.

ModelLevel.description: Fast: the runtime's smallest quick model; Balanced: its usual model; Smart: its most capable model (#2658).

MoveAnswer.description: What a person's move came to. The message is what the window may show.

MoveRequest.description: The person moving an agent (053). No target takes back the person's move that is waiting.

NativeSetting.description: A runtime's own setting for one level: config option values (mode, model, effort), a sandbox choice, or the answer to permission requests.

NeedID.description: NeedID (Attention/Need.swift): what is being answered, one key per kind. A notice (#2805) is what an agent told the person with `notify`: posted, never a Needs you row.

NoticeDelivered.description: notices/delivered (#2860): the control plane sent a host's notice to one of the person's devices.

NoticeDelivery.description: Where the notice recorded as entry `notice` went (#2860), recorded after it once the host knows: when it sends it to the computer, or when the control plane says which device it sent it to. A client draws it on that notice's line.

NoticeDevice.description: Where a notice went (#2860): the computer (the Mac window or the web page, the "mac" surface), an iPhone, an iPad, or a device of a kind the control plane does not know.

NoticeLimits.description: The person's attention (#2805, #2859): how many notices agents may send at once (burst, 1–20), and the minutes until one comes back (cooldownMinutes, 1–1440). The notifications part of the user settings, user/setNoticeLimits, and notices/take, which a host asks on its channel 0 before it posts a notice.

NoticeOutcome.description: What became of a notice an agent sent with `notify` (#2805): sent to where the person is, shown here (the person was looking at that chat), muted (#2003), or held in the cool-down.

NoticeTaken.description: notices/take (#2859): whether a notice may go now, from the one bucket the control plane keeps for the person and every machine of theirs: how many more can go now, and when the next comes back.

OTLPExport.description: The OTLP exporter of the report figures (#2019, #1804 decision 4), set on agents-control by OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, as this copy runs it: where it sends, the last send and the last failure.

OrgPolicy.description: The organisation's policy (#998, spec 998 FR-001, FR-002): one document, kept by the control plane at v1/policy.json, signed by its control key and sent to every machine that says host.policy/1. Each rule is optional; an absent rule sets no ceiling. Only an admin changes it. The control plane sets version, issued, changedBy and requires; stopAll and budgets.raises change only by policy/stopAll and policy/raise.

version.description: One more at each change. A machine refuses a lower one (FR-008).

requires.description: The capabilities a machine needs to follow this policy: host.policy/1, and one for each later rule (FR-014). A machine that lacks one starts no agent.

modeCeiling.description: The loosest mode, by ModeLooseness rank 0 to 4. A mode a machine does not know counts as rank 4.

sandbox.description: Required refuses the choice off and the states none and runtimeControlled. Absent is the person's choice.

runtimes.description: The runtimes allowed, by runtime id. Absent allows every runtime.

requireFollowing.description: The control plane refuses agent starts and prompts on a machine that has not applied this version.

groups.description: Empty. A place for later layers that only make a rule tighter.

OrgProvider.description: An org sign-in provider (#1002, D1, FR-001): an OIDC issuer that an organisation registered for this control plane. Kept at v1/signin/providers/<id>.json; its client secret is sealed beside it and never returned. The control plane sets version, secret, created, changed and redirectURI.

id.description: [a-z0-9-]{2,32}, made from the name when absent at add, never changed: the provider of each sign-in it makes.

name.description: On the button: Sign in with <name>. 1 to 40 characters.

issuer.description: An https URL. Its discovery document must name it as issuer.

accountClaim.description: The claim that names a person for life (D5): sub, or oid for Entra.

tenant.description: Entra: the tid an ID token must have.

redirectURI.description: The callback to register at the provider: this control plane's https address and /v1/oidc/callback. Only in answers.

scim.description: SCIM for this provider (slice 2a). Set by scim/set only.

OrgProviderCheck.description: signIn/orgProviders/check (#1002, FR-004): what the issuer's discovery document lacks, and how many keys its JWKS has.

OrgProviderJoin.description: Who may join through an org provider (D10): only people from SCIM, anyone the provider signs in, or only by invite.

OrgProviderKept.description: An org provider with its store tag, for an admin (#1002).

OrgProviderList.description: signIn/orgProviders/list (#1002): every org provider, for an admin. No secret.

OrgProviderPreset.description: Which form filled an org provider (#1002, research R3). Only googleWorkspace changes a check: hd must be a claimed domain.

OrgProviderSCIM.description: An org provider's SCIM (#1002, FR-013, FR-016): on or off, and the attribute that matches a provisioned person to a sign-in.

OrgProviderSecret.description: Who set an org provider's client secret, when, and its fingerprint: the first 8 hex of its SHA-256 (#1002, D4). Never the value.

OrgProviderSet.description: signIn/orgProviders/set (#1002, FR-001 to FR-004): add or change an org provider. secret is written only, never read back; needed to add. rev is the tag the admin read; none to add.

OrgRoute.description: An organisation's way to the model for one or more runtimes (#999, spec FR-001): an org key or a gateway. The control plane keeps it at v1/org/routes/<id>.json; its secrets are in an envelope beside it, never in this record. The control plane sets version, secretFields, fingerprint, created and changed; machines is how many machines hold its version, for an admin.

id.description: [a-z0-9-]{1,40}, made from the name when absent at add, never changed.

name.description: What members see, such as Acme Bedrock. 1 to 60 characters.

runtimes.description: The runtimes it serves: only those whose row of the spec's table allows the kind.

models.description: The runtime's model ids to the gateway's. Absent: the runtime's ids as they are.

groups.description: The groups whose people may use it (T1). Empty: everyone.

defaultFor.description: The runtimes whose default account it is.

secretFields.description: The names of the secret fields that are set (apiKey, awsAccessKeyId, serviceAccount, entraClientSecret, …), never a value.

fingerprint.description: The first 8 hex of SHA-256 of each secret value (spec D14), by field.

version.description: One more at each change, a replaced key included.

machines.description: How many machines said they keep this version (host/orgRoutesApplied). Only in orgRoutes/list.

OrgRouteCheck.description: orgRoutes/check (#999): what one small request from the control plane found, in words.

OrgRouteDelivery.description: host/orgRoutes (#999): every route the machine's person (or bot) may use. An empty list removes every route.

OrgRouteKept.description: An org route with its store tag, for an admin (#999).

OrgRouteKind.description: How an org route reaches the model (#999): an org key of the runtime's own vendor, or a gateway: Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, Microsoft Azure, or the organisation's own base URL.

OrgRouteList.description: orgRoutes/list (#999), an admin's: every route, and whether this control plane can seal a secret.

OrgRouteMine.description: A route the caller may use (#999): no settings, no fingerprint.

OrgRouteReplaceKey.description: orgRoutes/replaceKey (#999): new values for a route's secret fields.

OrgRouteRequest.description: orgRoutes/check and orgRoutes/remove (#999): a route, and for remove the tag the admin read.

OrgRouteSet.description: orgRoutes/set (#999): add a route, or change one. secrets are written only, never read back; an absent field keeps its value. rev is the tag the admin read; none to add.

OrgRouteSettings.description: An org route's settings that are not secret (#999, data-model.md). bedrock: region. vertex: folder, location. azure: resource or address, apiVersion, and tenant and clientID for an Entra app. baseURL: address, and header, the header the key goes in.

OrgRouteStamp.description: Who changed an org route, and when (#999).

OrgRouteVendor.description: An org route's vendor (#999): whose key a key route holds, and the API shape of a base-URL or Azure route.

OrgRouteVersion.description: A route a machine keeps, and its version (#999).

OrgRoutesApplied.description: host/orgRoutesApplied (#999): the routes a machine keeps, after a delivery.

OrgRoutesLeft.description: control/orgRoutesLeft (#999): a machine was removed with these routes on it. To its person and to every admin.

PRCostComment.description: What the host says on a folder's pull request when it merges (#2352): nothing (off, the default), the tokens and time only, or the cost too. Kept in the folder's .agents/folder.json, so the repo's people choose what a public repo publishes.

PairingCode.description: devices/startPairing: the Mac's relay key, a one-time secret and this Mac's name, good for five minutes or one device.

PairingSecret.description: pairing/current: the secret the bridge's listener should take, if any.

PassThroughName.description: One name in the person's own pass-through list (#998, FR-011a), as runtime-environment.json has it.

name.description: A variable's name, or a prefix ending in *.

runtime.description: The runtime it is passed to; absent for every runtime.

setBy.description: Set when the organisation's policy does not allow the name: it is not passed.

PassThroughState.description: settings/passThrough (#998): the person's own pass-through names, each marked when the policy refuses it.

PeopleChanged.description: control/peopleChanged (#994): a person was added, changed or removed.

PeopleList.description: people/list (#994): every user for an admin; for a member, only themselves.

PermissionLevel.description: Plan: reads and plans, changes nothing; Ask: asks before it changes things; Approve for me: does not ask for normal changes in its folder; Bypass Permissions: never asks, even for a change outside its folder (#2658, #2864).

PersonInvite.description: people/invite (#994): the new person's name and role.

PersonInvited.description: people/invite: the invite code to send, for one use within 7 days. Its first client pairs as the new person.

PersonMachine.description: A machine in People: its name, its state and nothing inside it (FR-019).

PersonRemovePreview.description: people/removePreview (FR-029, #1763): what Remove would take, for the admin to confirm. Started machines are stopped and deleted through their providers, each with the work on it that is not pushed; registered machines leave the control plane.

PersonRoleRequest.description: people/setRole (#994). Refused when it would leave no admin.

PersonRow.description: people/list (#994): a user, with their clients and machines.

spentTodayUSD.description: A bot's spend today, UTC, as its machines reported it (#1761).

scim.description: What SCIM says of the person, for one SCIM made (#1002). Shown as Managed by <provider>.

provisioned.description: Made by SCIM and not signed in yet: Waiting for first sign-in (#1002).

suspended.description: Suspended by their org provider (#1002, D13).

roleFrom.description: The SCIM groups that give the person their role (#1002, FR-020): Set by <provider>. Absent: set by hand.

PersonSCIM.description: What an org provider's SCIM says of a person (#1002, FR-015). The match is only inside its provider.

PersonSettings.description: What agents call the person, and their pronouns (#121), as given: person.json in the person's settings.

PersonSuspended.description: Why a person is suspended (#1002, D13): by SCIM, by a refresh the provider refused (Q1 A), or by an admin's id; with the provider and when.

PolicyApplied.description: host/policyApplied (#998): a machine kept this version of the policy.

PolicyBudgets.description: Each person's budget per UTC day and per agent (#998, FR-016): a ceiling over their own CostLimits. Money is US dollars.

allowUnmetered.description: Runtime ids that may run under a budget though their turns report neither a cost nor tokens.

raises.description: An admin's raises, each for one person and one UTC day.

PolicyEnvironment.description: The variable names a person's own pass-through list may name (#998, FR-011a), * at the end allowed.

PolicyHelpers.description: The ceiling over each folder's helper limits (#998, #64).

PolicyKept.description: policy/get and policy/set (#998): the whole policy with its store tag, for an admin. No policy and no rev when none was ever set. machines is each machine's applied version, by host id.

PolicyMarketplaces.description: The marketplaces a policy allows (#998), by the ids #687 gives them, and whether an MCP server added by hand is allowed.

PolicyNotices.description: The notices a policy decides for every member (#999, FR-008).

antigravityTerms.description: Google's terms notice for Antigravity: show (as absent), accepted (the organisation reviewed them; no notice), refuse (Antigravity is refused).

PolicyRaiseRequest.description: policy/raise (#998): an admin raises a person's budget for today (UTC).

PolicyReach.description: A way a runtime reaches the model (#999): the person's own sign-in, an org key, or a gateway.

PolicyRefusal.description: The data of a policyRefused error (#998, FR-010): why, the rule, and the words for the client.

PolicyRuntimeRule.description: One allowed runtime in a policy (#998).

models.description: The model ids allowed, with * at the end allowed (claude-sonnet-*). Absent allows every model.

reach.description: The ways this runtime may reach the model (#999). Absent: every way. [orgKey, gateway] is the org path only.

PolicySet.description: policy/set (#998): the rules, and the rev the admin read. No rev when there was no policy. Refused changedElsewhere when another admin saved first.

PolicySetBy.description: The mark on a choice a policy refuses or caps (#998, FR-010).

PolicySignature.description: The control key's signature of a policy (#998, FR-004), kept at v1/policy.sig: ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256 (es256), over the policy's canonical JSON (keys sorted, no spaces). sig is the 64 bytes r then s.

keyID.description: The first 8 bytes of the SHA-256 of the control key's X9.63 public key, base64url.

PolicyState.description: daemon/policyState and daemon/policyStateChanged (#998, T027): the organisation's policy as this machine follows it, so a client on the direct path draws the strip and the Policy pane. No version when this machine has no policy.

policy.description: The rules in force here, with only this machine's person's raises.

stopAll.description: The kill switch is on: this machine stops its turns and starts no work.

noPolicy.description: This machine had a policy from its organisation and has none it can trust now (missing, or it fails the signature check). It starts no work until it gets one.

update.description: The capabilities the policy requires that this machine lacks (FR-014). It starts no work.

refusal.description: Why this machine starts no work now, when it starts none.

PolicyStopAll.description: The kill switch (#998, FR-015): while on, every machine stops its turns and starts no work.

PolicyStopAllRequest.description: policy/stopAll (#998): the kill switch on or off, with an optional note.

PolicyView.description: policy/mine and control/policyChanged (#998): the policy in force, for any person, with only their own budget raises. No policy when none was ever set.

Project.description: A project (#2317): what people work on, the record that folders join. folders is what the machines last reported.

mayChange.description: The caller is the owner or an admin, so may rename and remove it, and set its slots.

slots.description: The project's Tasks, Code review and CI (#2669), one per slot: every folder in the project uses them. A slot that is not here is each folder's own.

ProjectFolder.description: A folder in a project (#2317), as its machine last reported it.

ProjectList.description: projects/list (#2317): the organisation's projects, by name.

ProjectRequest.description: projects/remove (#2317): the project. Refused while a folder names it.

ProjectSet.description: projects/set (#2317): makes a project, or with id renames one.

ProjectSlot.description: A project's Tasks, Code review or CI slot (#2669): the forge and the repository (GitHub owner/name, GitLab group/project) that fill it for every folder in the project, or skipped.

site.description: The repository's host: github.com, gitlab.com, or a self-managed GitLab's host.

skipped.description: Skipped for every folder in the project. forge, repository and site are then absent.

ProjectSlotSet.description: projects/setSlot (#2669): sets one of the project's slots, or with no value gives it back to each folder. Only the owner or an admin.

ProjectTools.description: One project's slots, as a machine gets them (#2669).

ProjectsChanged.description: control/projectsChanged (#2317): a project was made, renamed, adopted or removed, or a folder joined one.

ProjectsJoined.description: projects/joined (#2317): a machine's folders and the project each names, all of them each time.

voice.description: Sent from voice mode (#2322): the daemon puts the voice-mode text in front of the words, as the prompt's preface.

ProviderAdd.description: providers/add and providers/update. `secrets` only ever goes to the control plane; `cli` is not kept; `draft` is the draft this accepts (#858).

repository.description: The repository to start it from (#1809), an https git address. A provider whose New Machine form has `repository`, such as Codespaces, makes the workspace from it; any other has the host clone it once it joins, before `clones`.

ProviderDraftAnswer.description: providers/draftAnswer: yes or no to a question.

ProviderDraftAnswered.description: A draft answered with no agent: the server follows the contract, or a shipped map fits.

ProviderDraftUpdate.description: control/providerDraft: how a draft stands, to the client that started it.

ProviderGroup.description: providers/setGroup (#1761): the group whose users may use the provider. No group is the admins' alone.

ProviderOptions.description: providers/options: the New Machine form, a JSON Schema.

ProviderRuntimes.description: providers/runtimes: what may write, on which host, or why none.

ProviderSummary.description: A provider for the Providers page, never its commands, headers or secrets' values.

group.description: The group whose users may use it (#1761); none is the admins' alone.

mayUse.description: The caller may start machines from it (#1761): they are in its group. Absent from an older control plane, which lets everyone.

PushEnvironment.description: Which APNs a device token belongs to (#1460): a Debug build's (sandbox) or a TestFlight and App Store build's.

PushToken.description: clients/setPushToken (#1460): a device's own APNs token, in hex, for the control plane to push to when no Mac host relays its notices. No token takes it away.

ReadAPI.description: readApi/list (#2019), an admin's: the read API's tokens, newest first, revoked ones too; its URL; and the OTLP exporter when one is set.

ReadToken.description: A read API token (#2019, #1804 decision 4), with no value: the control plane keeps only its SHA-256. It reads the organisation's reports at /v1/read/reports, and nothing else.

ReadTokenMade.description: readApi/make (#2019): the token, its value once (never shown again), and the URL to read.

ReadTokenMake.description: readApi/make (#2019): a name for the token, such as the BI tool that uses it.

ReadTokenRevoke.description: readApi/revoke (#2019): the token to stop at once.

ReceiveRequest.description: Makes or brings up to date a host's copy of a Mac's repository (#1123): fetches the `bundle` upload, moves `branches` forward only, checks out `checkout`, sets `origin`, applies the `patch` upload (uncommitted changes), and adds the folder as a folder. It stops, and changes nothing, when the host has changes or commits of its own.

ReceiveState.description: What a host has at a folder before a send (#1123). `heads` are the commits of its branches, so the Mac's bundle carries only what the host lacks. `ownChanges` is true when the folder has changes that the last send did not put there.

ReceiveStateRequest.description: Asks a host about a folder a Mac will send a repository to (Send to ‹host›…, #1123). `folder` may start with ~/.

ReceiveUploadRequest.description: One part of a file a Mac sends (#1123), at `offset` in the upload. A part is at most 16 MB; the host keeps the upload until folders/receive uses it.

RelayCount.description: relay/count (#1163): one device's Needs you count, posted as a silent push.

RelayDelivery.description: relay/deliver (T097): seal the headline to `publicKey` and post it for `device`; no headline is a withdrawal.

RelayDevice.description: A device a relay host may carry for, with the key its frames are sealed to.

RelayRegistration.description: relay/register: the public half of the Mac's relay key, X9.63.

RelaySwitch.description: relay/switch (#824): the relay host that says it, on or off.

RelayTokens.description: The tokens the machine's model relay counted from the provider's own answers (#999, FR-019): fresh input, output, and cache reads and writes.

RemoveRequest.description: A Remove request (#1002, D13, FR-017): an org provider deleted a person by SCIM; the person is suspended, and an admin confirms the removal with people/remove.

RemoveRequestList.description: people/removeRequests (#1002): the Remove requests waiting for an admin, oldest first.

ReportCounts.description: What a machine's agents did in an hour or a day (#2019, R2 to R6), counted from its own event log and its time ledger: never a conversation's words. Absent from a machine before #2019.

sessions.description: Agents that began their first turn (agent.started).

failedSessions.description: Agents that ended in an error that nobody chose (agent.failed).

prsOpened.description: Pull and merge requests opened from an agent's branch on this machine (pr.opened).

prsReverted.description: Of those merged, the ones that revert another: a title that starts with "Revert".

mergeSeconds.description: The merged ones' time from their agent's start to the merge, added up: divide by prsMerged for the mean.

waits.description: The times an agent waited for its person in a turn (a question, a form, a permission).

waitBuckets.description: The waits by how long each was: under 1 minute, 5, 15, 60, 240, and longer. Six numbers.

workflowFailures.description: Runs whose agent ended in an error (agent.failed of an agent a workflow started).

ReportExport.description: reports/export's answer (#1811): the rows as CSV or JSON lines.

ReportPolicy.description: Who sees what in Reports (#1804), set by an admin in Console ▸ Report Policy.

totalsOnly.description: A group lead sees the group's totals only, with no person or machine named. An admin always sees each person.

leads.description: Each group's leads, by group id: users who see the group's reports.

budgetsUSD.description: A budget for a calendar month in US dollars, by group id, or "org" for the organisation.

ReportQuery.description: reports/usage and reports/export (#1811). With no scope, an admin sees every person and a member their own machines; a scope (#1804) is one the caller may see (reports/scopes).

scope.description: Me, a group or the organisation (#1804).

ReportRange.description: D is the last 24 hours by the hour; W, M and 3M the last 7, 30 and 90 days by the day (UTC).

ReportRow.description: One hour or day of one machine's folder and runtime, with its person (#1811).

workflow.description: The workflow that started the agents of this row (#2019), by its id; absent for agents a person or another agent started.

workingSeconds.description: The agent, its tools and waiting on others: TimeBucket's agent + tools + others.

waitingSeconds.description: Waiting for the person: TimeBucket's person.

groups.description: The groups the person is in (#1804), by id, for a group or organisation scope; absent when the person is hidden.

counts.description: What the agents did (#2019): sessions, pull requests and waits.

project.description: The project the folder is in (#2670), by id, as its machine last reported it (projects/joined); absent for a folder in no project.

projectName.description: The project's name, absent with project.

ReportScope.description: Whose rows a report adds up (#1804).

group.description: The group's id, for kind group.

ReportScopeKind.description: Me (the caller's own machines), a group's people, or every person (#1804).

ReportScopeOption.description: A scope the caller may see, with its name (#1804).

ReportScopes.description: reports/scopes' answer (#1804): Me, each group the caller leads (every group for an admin), and the organisation for an admin.

ReportValue.description: reports/value (#2351): what the work in a scope cost and what it delivered, from the lineage nodes that the scope's machines send (#2350). A node is in the range when it last changed in it, with its whole cost. total is the work on issues and PRs; waste is the PRs closed without a merge and merged reverts; unlinked is the turns with no issue or PR. perMergedPR is total by the PRs merged, by currency. leadTimeSeconds is the median of the issues' lead times. issues and milestones are the most costly first, at most 100 each; limited says there are more.

ReportValueRow.description: One issue or milestone on Reports ▸ Value (#2351): its cost rolled up from every machine in the scope, as lineage/cost adds it up, and how its PRs ended.

leadTimeSeconds.description: From the first work on it to its last PR merged; absent before a merge.

ReportView.description: A saved view of Reports (#2019, R8): a page with its scope, range and way to add up, kept for the person who saved it.

id.description: Given by the control plane; empty to save a new view.

by.description: The way the page adds up: person, folder, machine, runtime, group or workflow.

ReportViews.description: The caller's saved views of Reports (#2019), in the order they were saved.

RequiredCapabilities.description: What the control plane needs of a peer to route for it (#1748): a host without each of host is needsUpdate, and a client without each of client is answered -32008.

ResourceName.description: ResourceName (Model/Lease.swift): the name, trimmed and lower-cased, as a single string.

ResourceState.description: ResourceState (Daemon/DaemonAPI.swift), as its encode(to:) writes it (#116): every holder in `holds`, and the first again as `lease` for a reader from before counted holders. A host from before #116 sends only `lease`, so `holds`, `places` and `declared` may be missing.

RetentionSetRequest.description: retention/set. Without confirmed, a change that would delete agents at once is only described.

accountFolderVariable.description: The variable that names the folder its sign-in is kept in, for a runtime that can have more than one account (#840): CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME.

setupNote.description: Something one of the runtime's features needs on this host and lacks, with the step that fixes it (#1946). Only on the runtime's own sign-in row.

accountID.description: The added account this row is for (#840), or an org account (org:<route id>, #999); absent for the runtime's own sign-in.

tokensToday.description: An org account's tokens today on this host, as its model relay counted them from the provider's answers (#999, D12): fresh input, cache writes and output. Only on an org account's row.

setBy.description: Set when the organisation's policy does not allow this runtime here (#998, FR-010).

SCIMEmail.description: A SCIM user's email (RFC 7643 §4.1.2), to show only: never a sign-in.

SCIMMatch.description: Which SCIM attribute must equal an org sign-in's account claim for the two to be one person (#1002, D5, R5).

SCIMName.description: A SCIM user's name parts (RFC 7643 §4.1.1), kept as they came.

SCIMSet.description: scim/set (#1002): turn SCIM on or off for an org provider, and say which attribute matches a sign-in (externalId by default).

SCIMToken.description: A SCIM bearer token of one org provider (#1002, D12, FR-014), with no value: the control plane keeps only its SHA-256.

SCIMTokenList.description: scim/tokens/list (#1002): one provider's tokens, newest first, revoked ones too.

SCIMTokenMade.description: scim/tokens/make (#1002): the token, its value once (never shown again), and the SCIM base URL to give the provider.

SCIMTokenMake.description: scim/tokens/make (#1002): a name for the token, and when it ends, if ever. Refused while two are live.

SCIMTokenUse.description: When and from where a SCIM token was last used (#1002, D12), written at most once a minute.
