SSHHost.description: A server ssh knows by a name, for Add a Machine's server box (#610).

SSHHostsRequest.description: hosts/sshHosts (#610): with a destination, just that, as typed.

SaidMatch.description: A session that said the text, and the line it is on.

SaidSearchRequest.description: agents/said (#1585): the sessions whose prompts or replies hold the text, any case, in one folder when folder says.

SaidSearchResult.description: The sessions that said it, the most recently active first.

setBy.description: Set when the organisation's policy requires the command sandbox (#998): off is refused, and a runtime that cannot be put in a sandbox does not start.

SealedEnvelope.description: Envelope: HPKE (P-256, HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM) to one device's key. Nothing in it is legible but to that device.

SecretLeftOn.description: A machine that was removed with a secret on it (#1760, FR-026): change the secret where it was issued.

name.description: The machine's name when it was removed.

SecretsLeft.description: control/secretsLeft (#1760, FR-026): to the person's own clients, when one of their machines was removed with secrets on it.

SelfUpdate.description: How a Mac's host updates Agents Host to the release the control plane names, with no administrator (#2178).

release.description: The release the control plane named last; none until it names one.

message.description: Why it failed or cannot, in a sentence for the person.

SelfUpdateState.description: Where updating Agents Host is (#2178): upToDate, off (the person turned it off), downloading, waiting (ready; it waits for the last turn to end), restarting, failed (the next release named tries again), cannot (this copy cannot update itself, such as one in a folder only an administrator changes).

SendFacts.description: What the Send sheet shows (#1123): the local branches, the one checked out (none when detached), the origin, and whether anything is uncommitted.

SendFactsRequest.description: Asks this Mac's host about a repository to send (Send to ‹host›…, #1123).

SendFile.description: A file the host made for a send, read with folders/sendRead (#1123).

SendPack.description: What folders/sendPack made (#1123): each branch at its commit, the bundle (none when the receiving host has every commit) and the patch (none when nothing is uncommitted).

SendPackRequest.description: Makes what a send carries (#1123): a bundle of `branches` without the commits in `leavingOut` (the receiving host's), and with `includeChanges` a patch of the uncommitted changes, new files git does not ignore among them.

SendRead.description: A part of at most 1 MB (#1530). `end` is true for the last, and then the host removes the file.

SendReadRequest.description: One part of a file folders/sendPack made, from `offset` (#1123).

SentBranch.description: A branch the Mac sends, at the commit it has (#1123).

SentNotice.description: What an agent told the person with `notify` (#2805), on the record where it called it: the notification's words, what became of it, and, in the cool-down, when the next can go.

SessionCall.description: agents/fromStarter (#2927): the agent that started a session from another machine reads, messages, stops or archives it, or asks how it stands. The host answers only when from is the session's StartedFrom. The control plane writes from.machine and from.who; the asking host writes from.agent.

replace.description: With op message: replace the message of the starter's that waits, as message_session's replace.

SessionCallReply.description: What agents/fromStarter says (#2927): the words for the agent, the session's title, and how it ended, absent while it goes on.

SessionEnded.description: machines/sessionEnded through host/machines, then agents/endedElsewhere (#2927): a session started from another machine has ended, so its starter's wait_for_agents can wake. The host sends machine as the starter's machine; the control plane sends it on as the ended session's.

SetClientPermissionRequest.description: An agent's own answer to permission requests (#2658, FR-019); no mode follows Settings.

SetFolderProjectRequest.description: folders/setProject (#2317): the project id to write into the folder's .agents/folder.json.

SetLevelsRequest.description: Change a running agent's model level or permission mode on its own runtime (#2658): each is mapped as at its start. An Auto agent keeps its runtime.

SharedLook.description: Something the overview lists under Needs a look, and the page it opens.

item.description: What it is about: a skill, a server, a runtime's name.

app.description: The app's own, sent to every agent.

runtimeOnly.description: Set up in one runtime's own config and nowhere else.

path.description: Relative to `~/.agents`, or to a folder's `.agents`.

files.description: Its files, relative to its folder, for the detail's tree: at most 40.

SharedReach.description: What one runtime does with one thing: it gets it (how), uses its own copy at a path, is left out (why), has no way to take it, or is not measured yet (`"unchecked"`, or with a note).

SharedRequest.description: `personal/shared`'s params: none reads the person's `~/.agents`; `folder` reads that folder's `.agents` (#754), which has no per-runtime reach.

summary.description: The command and its first arguments, or the URL without its query.

clash.description: The runtimes with a server of this name in their own config, and that file.
The other copy of a skill of this name, left where it was.

managed.description: Where a lock says it came from (059); none for the person's own.

SharedSnapshot.description: `personal/shared` (054): what is in the person's `~/.agents` and which runtime gets each thing, for Settings ▸ Agent Configuration. Read from disk on every call. Nothing in it is a value from `mcp.json`: env and headers go by name only (FR-023).

laidOut.description: False for a copy of the app with no personal home (a scratch root), when everything else is empty.

runtimes.description: The installed runtimes with a rule, by name: the columns.

SignIn.description: One way a person signs in (#994, spec 736): `local` is the local owner's (codes, with the control plane's key), `code` an invite code redeemed; Google, Apple and GitHub come with #995.

SignInAdd.description: signIn/addToMe (#995, FR-005): a sign-in to add to the caller's person: an ID token made with signIn/providers' nonce, or a GitHub user access token.

SignInAsk.description: signIn/ask, on an `s:` connection (#2097): a browser pairs by approval. `account` is the email or GitHub login of one of the person's sign-ins; `name` is the browser's.

SignInConfigure.description: signIn/configure (#995, admins): turn a provider on or off, and set Google's allowed Workspace domains or GitHub's allowed organisations. What is left out stays as it was.

SignInDecide.description: signIn/approve, signIn/deny (#995). `code` is the code a browser shows, typed by the person: signIn/approve of a browser's request needs it (#2097).

SignInDecided.description: control/signInDecided (#995): how a request ended: approved, denied or expired.

SignInDiscover.description: signIn/discover (#1002, FR-011): the email a person typed.

SignInDiscovered.description: signIn/discover's answer: the org provider of a claimed domain that sends people there, or none. The same for an unknown domain and a domain with no switch.

SignInDomainClaim.description: signIn/domains/claim (#1002): a domain for one org provider.

SignInDomainList.description: signIn/domains/list (#1002): every claimed domain, for an admin.

SignInDomainPreview.description: signIn/domains/preview (#1002, FR-012): the people and the built-in sign-ins that Require would refuse.

SignInDomainPreviewPerson.description: A person that Require changes, with their sign-ins at the domain.

SignInDomainSet.description: signIn/domains/set (#1002, D8): a claimed domain's switches; an absent one stays. Either needs a proved domain.

SignInOrgProvider.description: An org provider on the sign-in screen (#1002, FR-003): its id, name and order, and nothing more.

SignInOrgStart.description: signIn/orgStart (#1002, D2): start an org provider's flow for this connection: pair (an `s:` connection) or addToMe (a paired client's). returnTo says where the browser comes back: agents://oidc (app) or the web page (web).

SignInOrgStarted.description: signIn/orgStart's answer: the /v1/oidc/start address to open in the browser. It ends after 10 minutes.

SignInPair.description: signIn/pair, on an `s:` connection (#995): the client's name and kind, and its provider's token: an ID token for google and apple, a user access token for github. The control plane checks it and forgets it (FR-008, FR-010).

SignInProvider.description: One sign-in provider (#995, spec 736 FR-004): google, apple or github. `on` is the admin's switch; `available` is false when this build has no client id for it, with `why`. `clientID` is the app's own, what a client signs in with (FR-012).

SignInProviders.description: signIn/providers, signIn/configure (#995): the providers. `challenge` (base64url) is what a client's nonce is made from on this connection: the hello's nonce on an `s:` connection, or a fresh one used once on a paired client's. The client makes the nonce itself, from the control key it trusts and the challenge (R2), so a token cannot be passed on to another control plane (FR-008, FR-011). `domains` (Google Workspace) and `organisations` (GitHub) are for admins only (FR-006). `orgProviders` are the org providers turned on, in order (#1002), first on every sign-in screen.

discover.description: A claimed domain sends people to its org provider: a client offers Use an Email (#1002, FR-011).

SignInRemove.description: signIn/removeFromMe (#995): an outside sign-in to take off the caller's person. The local owner's stays.

SignInRequest.description: signIn/requests, control/signInRequested (#995, FR-010): a new client that signed in with GitHub, waiting for Approve on one of the person's clients, with the code it shows. A browser's (provider `browser`, #2097) has the account typed as `login` and an empty `code`: the person types the code the browser shows.

SignInTicket.description: signIn/ticket (#1002, D3, FR-006): the ticket the callback gave, on the connection that started the flow, within 2 minutes, once. To pair, the client's name and kind too.

SignInTicketResult.description: signIn/ticket's answer: the client paired, or the sign-in added to the caller's person.

SignInWaiting.description: control/signInWaiting, on an `s:` connection (#995, FR-010): a GitHub sign-in waits for Approve on another client of the person, which shows the same code.

SignedPolicy.description: A policy and its signature (#998): what a machine receives and keeps in <root>/policy.json.

Simulator.description: An iOS simulator on a Mac host (#842): its UDID, its name, its system and whether it is booted.

SimulatorList.description: simulators/list: the host's simulators, booted first. Reason says why there are none to list, when a host has no simulators (not a Mac, no Xcode).

SimulatorRequest.description: simulators/boot and simulators/shutdown: one simulator, by its UDID.

SimulatorScreen.description: A booted simulator's screen as a JPEG, and its size in pixels.

SimulatorScreenRequest.description: simulators/screen: a booted simulator's screen, at most maxHeight pixels tall (1200 when left out).

SimulatorTapRequest.description: simulators/tap: a touch on a booted simulator's screen, where from 0 to 1 across (x) and down (y).

SpendCaps.description: Spend caps (#1761, spec 736 FR-033): a bot or a group stops starting work once its spend today (UTC) reaches one. None is no cap.

levels.description: The values in the shared words (#2658). With runtimeID auto, the daemon picks the runtime (FR-006).

accountID.description: The added account the session uses (#840); absent for the runtime's own sign-in.

voice.description: Started from voice mode (#2375): its first prompt asks for a short spoken reply, as agents/prompt's voice does.

startedFrom.description: An agent on another machine started it, through the control plane (#2887): its chat says who.

StartedFrom.description: The agent on another machine that started a session with start_session (#2887). The control plane writes machine and who; the asking host writes agent.

StartedMachinePreview.description: A started machine in people/removePreview: the branches and worktrees on it with work that is not pushed. `unknown` says why it could not be asked (offline, or it did not answer), and then `unpushed` is empty.

Surface.description: Surface (Attention/Surface.swift): a tagged object, `{ mac: {} }` or `{ device: "<uuid>" }`.

TeamBot.description: A bot on Console ▸ Team Workflows (#1804, M6): its group, caps and spend today, its machines, the workflows it ran and what runs now.

capped.description: It is at its own or its group's cap until midnight UTC.

TeamBotRun.description: An agent running on a bot's machine (#1804, M6), as the machine last listed it, for bots/stopRun. No title, nothing it said.

TeamTrigger.description: workflows/trigger and workflows/fire (#2011, spec 736 FR-035): a folder or control-plane event (a server's, such as github or a channel's) or a schedule that a runs-on: workflow's trigger matched. A machine sends it to the control plane, which sends it once to one of the bot's machines. workflow is the folder's name and the workflow's id; trigger, the same words on every machine that heard it; event, the event (none for a schedule); dueAt, a schedule's due time.

TeamTriggerFired.description: workflows/fire's answer: ran is true when the machine took the trigger (it runs it, or records why not, as for any trigger); false when it cannot take it here (no such workflow, or runs-on: does not match this machine), and the control plane tries another.

TeamTriggerSent.description: workflows/trigger's answer: taken is true when runs-on: names a bot, and the control plane sends the trigger once to one of its machines; false when it names none, and the machine goes on as before.

TeamWorkflowRuns.description: One workflow a bot ran in the last 7 days (#1804, M6): how many times, and when last.

TeamWorkflows.description: console/teamWorkflows' answer (#1804, M6): every bot, for an admin.

timeZone.description: The host's time zone, an IANA identifier such as America/Los_Angeles, that its hour and day stamps are in (#1267). Absent from a host too old to say: read as the viewer's own.

ToolCallContent.description: ToolCallContent (ACP/ToolCallContent.swift): the protocol's shapes, as sent. Anything else is written back as it came, so another `type` may arrive.

TranscriptEntryKind.description: One key, the kind's name, holding its fields. A kind this build does not know is kept whole and written back as it was read (TranscriptEntry+Coding.swift).

TurnPhase.description: Where a session's turn is, as its Live Activity says it (#1744): working; a question or an approval waiting on the person; done; ended cleanly but wanting the person, as Needs you in the sidebars (#1861); stopped on purpose, as Paused in the sidebars (#1869); or ended in error, as Unexpected stop; or gone (archived or deleted).

route.description: The org route the turn went through (#999).

relayTokens.description: The relay's count for an org account's turn, beside what the runtime reported (#999).

URLString.description: An absolute URL as text: URL in Swift.

UUID.description: Upper case, as Swift's uuidString writes it.

UnpushedWork.description: A worktree with work that is not pushed: commits ahead of its upstream (`ahead`), or on a branch with no upstream (`unmerged`, commits not on the base), and changes not committed (`uncommitted`).

timeZone.description: The host's time zone, an IANA identifier such as America/Los_Angeles, that its hour and day stamps are in (#1267). Absent from a host too old to say: read as the viewer's own.

UsageReport.description: reports/usage's answer (#1811): rows oldest first, by the hour for D and by the day otherwise.

admin.description: Whether the caller sees every person's machines.

scope.description: The scope the rows are of (#1804).

personsHidden.description: The rows say no person and no machine (#1804): a group lead's view when the policy says totals only.

groupNames.description: The name of each group the rows name (#1804).

budgetUSD.description: The scope's budget for a calendar month, in US dollars (#1804); absent when it has none.

monthSpentUSD.description: What the scope spent this calendar month (UTC), in US dollars, beside budgetUSD (#2057); absent when there is no budget.

UsageRollup.description: usage/rollup (#1811): a machine's hours and days that changed since it last sent them, sent each hour on its channel 0. The control plane keeps hours 7 days and days 90.

work.description: The lineage nodes whose banked cost or rollup links changed since the last send (#2350), each whole: the control plane keeps a machine's latest of each, 90 days.

UsageRollupPeriod.description: An hour ("2026-10-21T15") or a day ("2026-10-21"), in UTC, and its rows: the whole of that period on this machine, which replaces what was sent before.

UsageRollupRow.description: One folder and runtime's usage in an hour or a day (#1811), as a machine adds it up.

workflow.description: The workflow that started the agents of this row (#2019), by its id; absent for agents a person or another agent started.

workingSeconds.description: The agent, its tools and waiting on others: TimeBucket's agent + tools + others.

waitingSeconds.description: Waiting for the person: TimeBucket's person.

counts.description: What the agents did (#2019): sessions, pull requests and waits.

limitTokens.description: The row's tokens as the machine counts them for a limit (#998, FR-017): fresh input and output, no cache reads and no thoughts. Absent from an older machine, whose rows count as inputTokens + outputTokens.

route.description: The org route of this row's turns (#999, FR-021); absent for the person's own sign-in and accounts.

folder.description: The folder name, so the same repository on two machines adds up.

UserAgentConfig.description: Legacy agentConfig snapshot (#1760); new agent configuration uses per-file state in AgentConfigFiles (#2129).

UserPartHere.description: settings/userPart's answer (#1760): this machine's own part, for a client to set at the user scope with Use This Mac's. An MCP server with a token in clear is refused, so no secret goes into the user settings unsealed.

leftOut.description: What could not be taken, by name: a skill with files beside its SKILL.md.

UserPartRequest.description: settings/userPart (#1760): a part of the user settings, as this machine has it now.

UserRole.description: A user's role (#994, spec 736 FR-001): an admin manages people; a member sees only their own.

UserSecret.description: user/setSecret (#1760, FR-025): a secret the control plane keeps sealed, and sends only to its person's own machines. The value is never sent back to a client.

UserSecretName.description: A secret's name, as ${NAME} in mcp.json and NAME= in ~/.agents-secrets/secrets.env.

sealing.description: False when this control plane has no key to seal secrets with, and user/setSecret is refused.

UserSecretRow.description: One row of user/secretNames (#1760): a secret's name, never its value.

machines.description: The machines it was sent to.

leftOn.description: Machines removed with it on them, since it was last set.

UserSettings.description: user/settings (#1760, #2410): the person's settings that follow them to each of their machines. An omitted part has no value yet, but does not make that setting machine-local. The control plane does not read inside a part.

agentConfigFiles.description: Per-file agent configuration state (#2129), with tombstones and logical timestamps.

notifications.description: The person's notice limits (#2859), as a NoticeLimits.

UserSettingsChanged.description: control/userSettingsChanged (#1760): to the person's own clients, when a part or a secret changed, so a pane reads again.

UserSettingsPart.description: user/setSettings (#1760): one part set, or with a null value removed from the user scope.

UserSettingsPartName.description: A part of a person's user settings (#1760, #2410). Each part has one fixed scope: MCP servers, agent configuration, runtimes, cost limits and notices (#2859) follow the person. Resources belong to each machine.

UserSuspended.description: user/suspended (#1002, FR-018): to each machine of a suspended person, at hello before its settings and within 5 seconds of a change; off: true ends it.

ViewAsk.description: What a third-party server's view waits on before it is drawn: the person's Show (#191). The data of a viewNeedsShow failure.

ViewToolCallRequest.description: An agent's call of one of the agents server's tools that has a view, relayed with its token.

WakeSettings.description: Whether this Mac is kept awake for agents, and for how long after they stop (024), as wake.json in the root.

WakeState.description: Why the Mac is, or is not, being kept awake (024).

WebPushKey.description: clients/webPushKey (#1486): the control plane's VAPID public key, X9.63, base64url without padding, as pushManager.subscribe takes it. None when this control plane sends no Web Push.

WebPushSubscription.description: clients/setWebPush (#1486): a browser's push endpoint and its two keys, base64url, as PushSubscription.toJSON() gives them. No endpoint takes it away.

WireDate.description: Seconds since 2001-01-01T00:00:00Z: Date in Swift, through a plain JSONEncoder.

WorkOutcome.description: How a turn ended (#1916): only a question needs the person. A value this build does not know, such as an old record's `blocked`, `stuck` or `partly_done`, reads as `done`.

continueWhenBack.description: `continue-when-back: true`: a run's turn refused for a spent allowance waits for it at once, as if the person had chosen Continue (#1918).

muted.description: `muted: true`: every run of the workflow starts muted (#2003), and muting or unmuting the workflow mutes or unmutes its runs.

runsOn.description: runs-on: (#1761, FR-034), which replaced hosts:: labels a machine must all have to run it: its id, its os (macos, linux), its provider, and its user's or bot's name. None runs on every machine of each person who turned it on.

WorkflowClaim.description: workflows/claimRun (#1761, FR-034): a machine asks to run a runs-on: workflow for one trigger. The first to ask wins; the trigger is the same words on every machine that heard it.

WorkflowClaimed.description: workflows/claimRun's answer: won is false when another machine runs it.

WorkflowLimitSettings.description: How many approved workflows may be turned on in each folder. An unset value means 20. The range is 1 to 100. Kept in workflow-limit.json.

runsOn.description: runs-on: (#1761, FR-034), which replaced hosts:: labels a machine must all have to run it: its id, its os (macos, linux), its provider, and its user's or bot's name. None runs on every machine of each person who turned it on.

hearsFor.description: A bot's workflow that does not run here (#2027): the bot's name. This machine hears its server triggers with its own servers, once approved here, and sends each match to the control plane, which runs it on one of the bot's machines. Nothing of it runs here.

WorkflowSummary.description: Read forgivingly (Workflow.swift's init(from:)): a field that is missing or does not read takes its default (`isEnabled` true; false, 0, [] or absent for the rest).
